name: Museo Provincial La Periquera
overview: Provincial history museum in a National Monument on Parque Calixto García, Holguín (EcuRed, Spanish Wikipedia). EcuRed gives the address as Calle Frexes No. 198, between Libertad and Maceo.
EcuRed says the house was built from 1860 to 1868 for Francisco Rondán Rodríguez.
EcuRed says the name comes from the cry "Salgan de la jaula, pericos" shouted by besiegers in 1868, when Spanish forces and conservative families sheltered in the building.
funding_verdict: Museo Provincial La Periquera: state museum within Holguín's Centro Provincial de Patrimonio Cultural, a system subordinate to the Ministry of Culture (the centre's own site)

name: Teatro Sauto
overview: Neoclassical theatre in Matanzas, declared a National Monument by Resolution 003 of 10 October 1978 with protection grade I (EcuRed).

EcuRed dates the opening to 6 April 1863, after a fund drive among landowners, merchants and property owners. It says Francisco de Albear approved two of six competition entries and the Italian Daniel Dall'Aglio's design was chosen from them.
First named Teatro Esteban for governor Pedro Esteban Arraz, later Colón, Martí and La Vigía, then Sauto for the pharmacist and arts patron Ambrosio de la Concepción Sauto y Noda (EcuRed).
funding_verdict: Teatro Sauto: built in 1863 with money from landowners, merchants and property owners; the national heritage council prized its restoration and the provincial culture directorate spoke for its programme

press_items.title: Julio César Contreras, "La 'Atenas de Cuba' se ha convertido en un desierto cultural" (2024)

name: Museo Provincial de Pinar del Río
overview: Provincial history museum at Calle Martí No. 58, between Recreo and Colón, on Pinar del Río's main street (EcuRed).
EcuRed says it opened on 14 December 1979 with one room and the remaining rooms followed on the same date in 1981, giving five permanent halls and one temporary hall.

The eclectic building with Moorish influence stands on land sold in 1883 to Dr Agustín Antón, who built two masonry houses. The Diputación Provincial bought them in 1892 and the provincial government sat there until 1959 (EcuRed).
funding_verdict: Museo Provincial de Pinar del Río: state museum in the network of the Pinar del Río provincial heritage centre (EcuRed), within the Ministry of Culture's heritage system

name: Museo del Humor
overview: Museum of graphic humour on Calle 60 at the corner of Calle 45 in San Antonio de los Baños, Artemisa province, 37 km from Havana (EcuRed).
EcuRed says the idea came in March 1978 at the First Forum of Humorists and the museum opened on 17 March 1979 as the Museo Internacional del Humor.
The house was built in 1830 by the Marquis of Campo Florido, in stone and hardwood with Spanish tile roofs and marble floors, and was declared a local monument in 1980 (EcuRed).
funding_verdict: Museo del Humor: state museum with the Ministry of Culture as parent body (EcuRed); state bodies co-sponsor its Bienal

press_items.title: Redacción OnCuba, "Desde este domingo, Bienal Internacional de Humorismo Gráfico en Cuba" (2023)
Redacción OnCuba, "Bienal Internacional de Humor Gráfico en marcha en Cuba con Irán como protagonista" (2025)

name: Museo Castillo del Morro San Pedro de la Roca
overview: Fortress at the entrance of Santiago de Cuba's bay, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list on 6 December 1997 under criteria iv and v, on a 94-hectare property (EcuRed, state encyclopedia, archive copies of 29 March and 3 June 2025).

Construction began in 1638 under the governor Pedro de la Roca y Borjas, after a visit by the Italian military engineer Juan Bautista Antonelli; an English attack destroyed it in 1662 and it was rebuilt and enlarged between 1663 and 1669 (EcuRed).
Used as a military prison in the independence war; Bartolomé Masó, Flor Crombet and Emilio Bacardí Moreau were among the prisoners (EcuRed; Havana Times).
funding_verdict: Museo Castillo del Morro San Pedro de la Roca: public: Cuban state property, managed by the provincial heritage centre

name: Museo Provincial Emilio Bacardí Moreau
overview: Provincial museum in the historic centre of Santiago de Cuba, on Pío Rosado (Carnicería) between Aguilera and Heredia (OnCuba).

Opened on 12 February 1899 as the Museo Municipal, set up by a group of Santiago patriots with Emilio Bacardí, then mayor, and Elvira Cape. Its first seat was a rented house at Santo Tomás 25, and it moved several times (OnCuba, Sierra Maestra). Sierra Maestra calls it the oldest public institution of its type in Cuba.
Named for Emilio Bacardí Moreau, elected Santiago's first mayor, writer, and officer of the Liberation Army, whom Spain imprisoned twice (OnCuba).
funding_verdict: Museo Provincial Emilio Bacardí Moreau: mainly public: Ministry of Culture heritage system

press_items.title: Igor Guilarte, "El museo de las mil y una historias en Santiago de Cuba" (2024)

name: Museo Romántico de Trinidad
overview: Museum of decorative arts in the Palacio Brunet, Calle Fernando Hernández Echerry 52 at Simón Bolívar, on the Plaza Mayor of Trinidad, Sancti Spíritus province (EcuRed; Spanish Wikipedia).
Trinidad's historic centre has been on the UNESCO World Heritage list since 1988 (Prensa Latina; Spanish Wikipedia).
The ground floor dates from 1740; José Mariano Borrell y Padrón bought the house in 1807 and added the upper floor in 1808 (EcuRed; Spanish Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Museo Romántico de Trinidad: mainly public: the Ministry of Culture's heritage system, with its own ticket revenue

name: Jurkovič Villa
overview: Villa at Jana Nečase 2 in Brno-Žabovřesky, at the foot of the Wilson Forest (Czech Wikipedia).
The architect Dušan Jurkovič built it in 1906 for himself, and it is named for him. It opened on 26 August 1906 as an exhibition venue before he moved in, and he sold it in 1919 (Czech Wikipedia).
Secession style built on the British cottage plan, with a central staircase hall linking the ground-floor social rooms to the private part upstairs (Czech Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Jurkovič Villa: mainly public: Czech state through the Moravian Gallery, with a Norwegian grant

name: Villa Stiassni
overview: Villa at Hroznová 14 in the Pisárky district of Brno, in gardens of more than three hectares (stated by the villa's site).
Built 1927 to 1929 for the Jewish textile factory owner Alfred Stiassni and his wife Hermine, and named for the family (Brno Architecture Manual, Deník).
Architect Ernst Wiesner: reinforced concrete pillars carry two stepped wings, with stucco, coffered ceilings and marble fireplaces inside (Brno Architecture Manual).
funding_verdict: Villa Stiassni: mainly public: Czech state and EU grant money through the National Heritage Institute

name: Villa Tugendhat
overview: Villa at Černopolní 45 in Brno, a department of the Brno City Museum (villa's site).
Ludwig Mies van der Rohe built it in 1929 to 1930 for Greta and Fritz Tugendhat, and it is named for them. It has been on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2001 (villa's site).
The Tugendhats lived there about eight years and fled in 1938. The villa became city property after the war (English Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Villa Tugendhat: mainly public: the City of Brno through the Brno City Museum

press_items.title: Russell Fortmeyer, "Less is More to Restore at Mies' Tugendhat Villa" (2007)
no author named, "40 let od rekonstrukce vily Tugendhat" (undated, announces events from 13 August 2025)

name: Bauer Villa
overview: Cubist villa at Libodřice 111 in the Kolín district (upm.cz).
Josef Gočár designed it for the landowner Adolf Bauer and it was built in 1912 to 1914. It is named for the Bauer family (upm.cz).

Bauer died in 1929. In 1940 the villa was confiscated as Jewish property and came under German administration, and the Bauer family died in the Holocaust. It was nationalised in 1948 and added to the Central List of Cultural Monuments in 1987 (upm.cz, Seznam Zprávy).
funding_verdict: Bauer Villa: mainly public: the Ministry of Culture bought it and the Museum of Decorative Arts runs it

name: Brummel House (Adolf Loos in Pilsen)
overview: Privately owned house at Husova 58 in Pilsen, near the bus station. It is the only Loos building in Pilsen still in private hands (adolfloosplzen.cz, brummeluvdum.cz, CzechCrunch).

Adolf Loos and Karel Lhota redesigned an older house in 1928 to 1929 for Jan Brummel, his wife Jana and her mother Hedvika Liebsteinová. The house is named for the Brummel family (brummeluvdum.cz, CzechCrunch).

The Brummels were deported during the war and the Nazi Adolf Straub lived there. After nationalisation the house was split into rented flats, and from 1962 it housed the Club of Architects (CzechCrunch).
funding_verdict: Brummel House: privately owned: family money, with city support and state-funded tours

name: Semler Residence
overview: Apartment of the Oskar Semler family at Klatovská 110 in Pilsen, in a building put up in the early 1920s for Škoda clerks (semler.cz).

Oskar and Jana Semler bought it in the early 1930s and remodelled part of it as their apartment in 1932 to 1934. Adolf Loos took part in the basic concept, and Heinrich Kulka worked it out and completed the building. Loos died in 1933 (semler.cz, Gallery of West Bohemia via iUmění).
The residence is named for the Semler family. They left in 1939, the Nazis confiscated the house and the Czechoslovak state took it over after 1945 (semler.cz).
funding_verdict: Semler Residence: mainly public: Plzeň Region, with EU money for the restoration

name: Villa Bílek
overview: Home and studio of the sculptor František Bílek at Mickiewiczova 233/1 in Hradčany, Prague 6, a few minutes' walk from Hradčanská metro station or Prague Castle (Prague City Gallery, English Wikipedia).
Bílek built it in 1910 to 1911 to his own plans, and the house is named for him (Prague City Gallery).

Brickwork articulated by pillars in the form of corn sheaves (English Wikipedia). ArtRevue calls the pillars concrete, Egyptian-style columns shaped like ears of grain, set against dark brickwork. His first, ruin-like design had to be simplified after objections from the building office (ArtRevue).
funding_verdict: Villa Bílek: mainly public: the City of Prague through the Prague City Gallery

name: Villa Müller
overview: Villa at Nad Hradním vodojemem 642/14 in Střešovice, Prague 6 (Museum of Prague).

Adolf Loos and Karel Lhota designed it for František Müller, co-owner of the construction firm Kapsa and Müller, and his wife Milada. It was completed in 1930 and is named for the family (English Wikipedia, CzechCrunch).
The communists seized it in 1948. The Müllers' daughter Eva Maternová sold it to the City of Prague in 1995, and it opened as a museum in 2000 (English Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Villa Müller: mainly public: the City of Prague through the Museum of Prague

name: Villa Rothmayer
overview: House museum at U Páté baterie 896/50, Prague 6, Břevnov, on the border with Střešovice near the Central Military Hospital (Museum of Prague; Expats.cz).

The architect Otto Rothmayer built it as his family home in 1928 and 1929 from concepts by Jože Plečnik, whose student and collaborator he was at Prague Castle and Lány Castle; it is named for him (Expats.cz).
His wife, the textile artist Božena Rothmayerová, had her study there, and the spiral staircase carries artefacts he brought home from Prague Castle (Museum of Prague).
funding_verdict: Villa Rothmayer: mainly public: the City of Prague through the Museum of Prague

name: Zikmund Villa
overview: Villa at Žlebová 2894 in the Nivy district of Zlín, a cultural monument (villa's site).

Built in 1934 to 1935 by the Baťa support fund as a service flat for Zlín's first district governor, Josef Januštík. In 1942 the film director Elmar Klos bought it. His parents lived there until 1953, when they were forced out of the town (foundation annual report 2025).

Klos sold it to the traveller Miroslav Zikmund, for whom it is named. Zikmund rebuilt it with the architect Zdeněk Plesník and the designer Miroslav Navrátil and lived there almost 70 years (annual report 2025).
funding_verdict: Zikmund Villa: owner-funded foundation: the founder's own foundation, NAVI CZ, PSG Construction and other firms, private donors and EEA and Norway Grants

name: Musée des Cultures Contemporaines Adama Toungara (MuCAT)
overview: Museum of contemporary art in the Abobo commune of Abidjan, on 3,500 m² opposite the Abobo town hall (Connectionivoirienne, 11 March 2020).

Named for Adama Toungara, identified in 2020 as the Grand Médiateur de la République and one of the country's largest art collectors. Inaugurated on 11 March 2020 by First Lady Dominique Ouattara (Connectionivoirienne, 11 March 2020).

Built through the Adama Toungara Foundation (Connectionivoirienne, 29 February 2020). Connectionivoirienne calls it the first building in Côte d'Ivoire dedicated to contemporary culture. Fraternité Matin (30 June 2021) calls it the first museum entirely dedicated to contemporary art.
funding_verdict: Musée des Cultures Contemporaines Adama Toungara: privately funded: the Adama Toungara Foundation

name: Texaf Bilembo
overview: Cultural and educational space in Kinshasa, in the Nouvelle Concession UTEX on rue Esengo, with its entrance at 372 Avenue Colonel Mondjiba, Gombe commune (Kino Congo). The centre's own site gives the address as Rue Esengo (Utexafrica).
Inaugurated on 7 November 2013. Conceived by art historian Chantal Tombu, writer and photographer Alain Huart and artist Christine Decelle (stated by the centre).
Texaf, the Brussels-listed company, founded the space and is its main patron. Former Texaf chief executive Philippe Croonenberghs gave the site to the project (stated by the centre).
funding_verdict: Texaf Bilembo: corporate-funded: Texaf, a Brussels-listed Congolese property and quarry group, is founder and head sponsor

name: Museo de la Palabra y la Imagen (MUPI)
overview: Museum and archive of Salvadoran memory at 27 Avenida Norte #1140, Urbanización La Esperanza, San Salvador (museum website).

Founded by the Venezuelan journalist Carlos Henríquez Consalvi, who is also its director. Wikipedia says the late 1990s, the museum's own timeline shows it appearing publicly in 1996 with the book "Luciérnagas en El Mozote" and the campaign "Contra el caos de la desmemoria," and El Salvador's press marked its 30th anniversary in January 2026.
The name means Museum of the Word and the Image.
funding_verdict: MUPI: donor-funded: private non-profit supported by foreign development funders and public donations
